A.title: A Digital Audience: Five Ways People Build a Public Profile
A.text:
Many young adults would like their work to reach a large audience. Digital services have made it possible to share videos, photographs and writing without asking a television station or newspaper for permission. However, being noticed is not automatic. People still need to make useful material, post regularly and treat other users respectfully.

CLIPSTREAM is a video-sharing service. Film-makers can upload short clips, music lessons and longer documentaries. One young creator, Maya, became known for explaining simple science experiments. Her videos are watched by students in several countries. She now earns money through advertising, although most people who upload videos earn very little.

PHOTOSQUARE focuses on pictures. It is particularly useful for photographers who want to show a portfolio of their best work. Users can add short descriptions and answer questions about the pictures. A beautiful photograph may attract attention, but the service is less suitable for teaching a complicated skill step by step.

TALKLINE allows users to send very short written updates. Community organisers use it to announce local events and answer questions quickly. A message can spread widely within a few hours. Yet the short format sometimes makes serious issues difficult to explain accurately. I believe people should check a claim before sharing it with others.

YOUR OWN BLOG offers more control. A blogger can publish detailed articles about a specialist subject, such as repairing bicycles, cooking or protecting local wildlife. A thoughtful article may not receive much attention immediately, but a collection of useful posts can build trust over time. Blogs often require patience and regular editing.

SKILLCAST is designed for practical demonstrations. Teachers and experts make step-by-step courses and answer learners' questions. Some courses are free; others charge a small fee. The platform is helpful for people who want to teach a skill, but it does not promise its users fame. Whichever service they use, creators are more likely to keep an audience if their information is reliable.

B.title: A Little Fame in a Small Town
B.text:
I run a small community radio programme, so a few people in my town recognise my voice. At first, I enjoyed every conversation with listeners. Last month, someone interrupted my dinner to ask about a guest on the show. I answered politely, but I felt uncomfortable because I wanted to spend time with my family.

My work has also given me wonderful opportunities. I have met interesting people and helped local charities explain their projects. I would not want to become a national celebrity, however. I value being able to walk through town without strangers taking photographs. Perhaps fame is pleasant for some people, but I am happier with a quiet life.

C.title: Animals That Changed the Way People Think
C.text:
A. Animals may become well known because they appear in films, help people, or inspire a community. Their fame can create interest in wildlife and animal welfare. It can also lead to crowded visitor sites, so carers have to consider the animal's comfort.

B. In a seaside town, a dog named Rowan waited outside the railway station each afternoon for a worker who regularly gave him food. When the worker moved away, the dog continued visiting the same place for several years. Local residents looked after Rowan and later placed a small bronze statue near the station. They hold a short remembrance event each spring. There is no evidence that Rowan ever travelled by train.

C. An orphaned bear cub named Nilo was rescued after a forest fire. The cub was taken to a wildlife centre, where carers helped it recover. Visitors followed its progress through short online updates. Donations to the centre rose, and the extra funds paid for food and improved enclosures. Nilo was later transferred to a larger protected area. The centre refused requests to allow tourists to hold the bear because staff wanted to protect its health.

D. A young lioness called Zuri became famous after appearing in a documentary about habitat loss. The film showed how roads and fences can divide wild animals' territory. Viewers supported a programme to create safe routes between protected areas. Zuri was not trained for a circus or kept as a household pet. The filmmakers avoided getting close to her and used distant cameras.

E. Fame is not always positive for animals. Online pictures can help people understand a species, but they can also encourage visitors to behave carelessly. Responsible programmes focus on protecting habitats and keeping animals safe rather than simply attracting attention. It is human organisations that usually receive the financial rewards from an animal's popularity.

A.title: Career of a documentary creator
dialogue: NARRATOR
Today I am going to describe how a young film-maker, Iris Chen, built an online audience.
NARRATOR
Iris began by learning photography at school. Later, she taught herself video editing by working on short projects.
NARRATOR
Her first public video was about a community garden. She entered a local film competition and won second prize.
NARRATOR
After that, she posted one new video every Friday. Her clear explanations and friendly style attracted thousands of viewers.
NARRATOR
A local newspaper interviewed her, but she did not sign a television contract. Instead, she started a small production company.
NARRATOR
Today she makes short documentaries for museums and charities. She says her success came from regular practice, not from overnight luck.

B.title: Two opinions about public attention
dialogue: MIA
I would not want to be famous. I would probably lose my privacy. People might photograph me when I was shopping, and I would find that stressful.
LEO
I feel differently. If I became well known for my music, I could perform in large theatres and meet other musicians.
MIA
But you might have to travel constantly and miss time with your friends.
LEO
That is possible. Still, I would use the money to support my family, and I would donate some of it to a music school.
MIA
I would prefer to have a normal job and spend quiet weekends with the people I love.

C.title: Four steps for creating a trustworthy blog
dialogue: PRESENTER
First, choose a subject you know well, such as gardening or local history. It is important to find something you genuinely enjoy.
PRESENTER
Next, study your audience. Read their questions carefully and plan articles that solve real problems.
PRESENTER
Then create a simple publishing schedule. You do not need to post every day, but you should be consistent.
PRESENTER
After each article, check your facts and give credit to your sources. Reliable information is more valuable than a shocking headline.
PRESENTER
Finally, learn from feedback. If you make a mistake, correct it openly rather than hiding it.

D.title: Basic camera techniques for an interview
dialogue: TECHNICIAN
Many cameras have automatic settings, but today we will look at manual controls.
TECHNICIAN
The focus ring is useful when the subject is close to the camera. Turn the ring slowly until the face looks sharp.
TECHNICIAN
The aperture controls the amount of light entering the lens. A wider opening allows more light through.
TECHNICIAN
If you film in a dark room, the image may appear brighter with a wider aperture. Be careful, though, because the background can become less sharp.
TECHNICIAN
For a long interview, use a tripod. This helps you avoid shaky pictures.
TECHNICIAN
The zoom control can make the subject appear closer, but too much zoom often makes small movements more obvious.
TECHNICIAN
Before recording, check that the microphone works and the battery is fully charged.

E.title: Planning a short film
dialogue: LECTURER
Before you make a short film, decide who the audience will be. A film for young children needs a different style from one for adults.
LECTURER
Second, write a simple story outline. Make sure the story has a clear beginning, middle and ending.
LECTURER
Next, decide on your budget. Even a school project may need money for travel, costumes and equipment.
LECTURER
Prepare a script that explains each scene, where the scene takes place and what the actors say.
LECTURER
Then draw a storyboard. This is a series of simple pictures showing the main shots.
LECTURER
Choose a director to make decisions during filming, and invite actors who are interested in the story.
LECTURER
Finally, arrange a rehearsal before recording the first scene.

F.title: Speaking Part 2 model: a person I admire
dialogue: CANDIDATE

I would like to talk about a science communicator I admire. Her name is Lan, and she makes short educational videos about everyday technology. I first saw her work about two years ago when a friend shared one of her videos.
CANDIDATE
She became well known because her explanations are clear and she uses simple demonstrations. What I like most is that she checks her sources carefully and corrects mistakes when she notices them.
CANDIDATE

I admire her for three reasons. First, she makes difficult information easy to understand. Second, she encourages young people to ask questions instead of believing every post they see. Finally, she seems kind to her audience and takes their questions seriously.
CANDIDATE
I have learned to be more careful about information on social media because of her. If I had a chance to meet her, I would thank her for making science enjoyable.

G.title: Speaking Part 3 models: celebrity culture
dialogue: EXAMINER
Why do some people become interested in celebrities?
CANDIDATE
I think famous people can be entertaining, and they sometimes inspire others to learn a new skill. However, too much attention to their private lives can be unhealthy.
EXAMINER
How has fame changed because of the internet?
CANDIDATE

In the past, newspapers and television controlled much of the attention. Now an ordinary person can reach a large audience through a useful video or article, although staying popular can be difficult.
EXAMINER
Should famous people have more privacy?
CANDIDATE
Yes, particularly when their children are involved. Public interest does not mean that every private moment needs to be photographed.

items.question_vi: Con vật làm tăng quyên góp?
items.explanation_en: The wildlife centre received more donations after Nilo’s updates.
items.explanation_vi: Quyên góp cho trung tâm tăng sau các bài về Nilo.

items.question_en: 5 Which animal visited a station repeatedly? A Rowan B Nilo C Zuri
items.question_vi: Con vật thường đến nhà ga?
items.explanation_en: Rowan returned to the station repeatedly.
items.explanation_vi: Rowan quay lại ga nhiều lần.

items.question_en: 6 Which animal was filmed using distant cameras? A Rowan B Nilo C Zuri
items.question_vi: Con vật được quay từ xa?
items.explanation_en: Film-makers used distant cameras for Zuri.
items.explanation_vi: Đoàn phim quay Zuri bằng máy từ xa.

items.question_en: 7 Which animal was later moved to a larger protected site? A Rowan B Nilo C Zuri
items.question_vi: Con vật chuyển tới khu bảo tồn rộng hơn?
items.explanation_en: Paragraph C explicitly describes the transfer.
items.explanation_vi: Đoạn C nêu rõ việc chuyển nơi sống.

items.question_en: 8 Every animal becomes famous through film. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Mọi con vật nổi tiếng nhờ phim?
items.explanation_en: Paragraph A lists films, help and community inspiration.
items.explanation_vi: Đoạn A có nhiều nguyên nhân khác nhau.

items.question_en: 9 Rowan travelled by train daily. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Rowan đi tàu mỗi ngày?
items.explanation_en: The passage says no evidence Rowan ever travelled by train.
items.explanation_vi: Bài nói không có bằng chứng Rowan từng đi tàu.

items.question_en: 10 Rowan’s statue is made of silver. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Tượng Rowan làm bằng bạc?
items.explanation_en: Paragraph B explicitly calls it bronze.
items.explanation_vi: Tượng làm từ đồng, không phải bạc.

items.question_en: 11 A remembrance event for Rowan is held in spring. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Có lễ tưởng niệm Rowan vào mùa xuân?
items.explanation_en: Residents hold an event each spring.
items.explanation_vi: Cư dân tổ chức mỗi mùa xuân.

items.question_en: 12 Nilo was held by visitors for photographs. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Khách được bế Nilo để chụp ảnh?
items.explanation_en: The centre refused requests to hold the bear.
items.explanation_vi: Trung tâm từ chối cho khách bế gấu.

items.question_en: 13 The Nilo centre has twelve employees. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Trung tâm Nilo có 12 nhân viên?
items.explanation_en: No staff total appears.
items.explanation_vi: Không có số nhân viên.

items.question_en: 14 Zuri was kept as a house pet. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Zuri được nuôi làm thú cưng?
items.explanation_en: Paragraph D explicitly denies that.
items.explanation_vi: Đoạn D phủ định rõ.

items.question_en: 15 Zuri’s documentary encouraged a wildlife programme. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Phim Zuri khuyến khích chương trình bảo tồn?
items.explanation_en: Viewers supported safe routes between protected areas.
items.explanation_vi: Người xem hỗ trợ chương trình hành lang an toàn.

items.question_en: 16 Animals normally receive the money their fame generates. YES/NO/NOT GIVEN
items.question_vi: Động vật thường trực tiếp nhận tiền từ danh tiếng?
items.explanation_en: The passage says human organisations usually receive it.
items.explanation_vi: Bài khẳng định tổ chức con người thường nhận tiền.

activities.title: Lead-in: media and celebrity words
activities.instruction_en: Identify nouns (things/people) and adjectives.
activities.instruction_vi: Phân biệt danh từ chỉ người/vật và tính từ.

items.question_en: “paparazzi” is: people / adjective / thing?
items.question_vi: Paparazzi là loại từ gì?
items.explanation_en: It means photographers who follow famous people.
items.explanation_vi: Chỉ nhóm thợ săn ảnh.

items.question_en: “talented” is: person / adjective / thing?
items.question_vi: Talented là gì?
items.explanation_en: It describes an ability.
items.explanation_vi: Tính từ mô tả có tài.

items.question_en: “reporter” is: person / adjective / thing?
items.question_vi: Reporter là gì?
items.explanation_en: A reporter is a journalist.
items.explanation_vi: Reporter là phóng viên.

items.question_en: “website” is: person / adjective / thing?
items.question_vi: Website là gì?
items.explanation_en: It refers to an online site.
items.explanation_vi: Chỉ một trang web.

items.question_en: “well-known” is: person / adjective / thing?
items.question_vi: Well-known là gì?
items.explanation_en: It describes somebody known to many.
items.explanation_vi: Tính từ chỉ được biết đến rộng rãi.

activities.title: Understand a body paragraph
activities.instruction_en: Identify the strengths and weaknesses of an advantages paragraph.
activities.instruction_vi: Tìm ưu điểm và điểm cần cải thiện của đoạn nói về lợi ích.

items.question_en: Which sentence is a topic sentence? A Fame can bring several benefits. B Some singers wear black clothes.
items.question_vi: Câu chủ đề hợp lý?
items.explanation_en: The sentence introduces the whole paragraph.
items.explanation_vi: Câu bao quát ý cả đoạn.

items.question_en: Which is more specific evidence? A Fame is nice. B A musician can raise funds for school instruments.
items.question_vi: Ví dụ nào cụ thể?
items.explanation_en: It names an action and beneficiary.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu rõ hành động và đối tượng nhận lợi ích.

items.question_en: Is repeating “famous” five times good cohesion? YES/NO
items.question_vi: Lặp famous 5 lần có tốt không?
items.explanation_en: Use pronouns and accurate synonyms to avoid repetition.
items.explanation_vi: Dùng đại từ và từ thay thế đúng nghĩa.

items.question_en: Why should an advantage connect back to the question?
items.question_vi: Vì sao luận điểm cần bám câu hỏi?
items.answer: To show its relevance to the essay task.
items.explanation_en: A body paragraph must support the main argument.
items.explanation_vi: Thân bài phải hỗ trợ luận điểm trung tâm.

activities.title: Claim–reason–example–result
activities.instruction_en: Match support to each main point.
activities.instruction_vi: Ghép luận điểm với lý do, ví dụ và kết quả.

items.question_en: Main point: celebrities can help charities. Choose: A ticket sales pay for a community library B singers are tall.
items.question_vi: Chọn bằng chứng cho lợi ích từ thiện.
items.explanation_en: Donation example directly illustrates the point.
items.explanation_vi: Ví dụ tiền vé giúp thư viện trực tiếp hỗ trợ ý.

items.question_en: Main point: fame reduces privacy. Choose: A fans take photos during private meals B a person likes music.
items.question_vi: Chọn bằng chứng cho thiếu riêng tư.
items.explanation_en: Private moments are interrupted by photographs.
items.explanation_vi: Ảnh chụp lúc ăn riêng tư thể hiện vấn đề.

items.question_en: Main point: public criticism causes stress. Choose: A harsh comments spread online B a large home is expensive.
items.question_vi: Chọn bằng chứng cho áp lực.
items.explanation_en: Online criticism provides relevant mechanism.
items.explanation_vi: Bình luận tiêu cực là nguyên nhân đúng chủ đề.

items.question_en: Order the paragraph: example → claim → reason → result. What comes first?
items.question_vi: Thứ tự đoạn: ví dụ → luận điểm → lý do → kết quả; gì trước?
items.explanation_en: An early claim guides the reader.
items.explanation_vi: Mở bằng luận điểm giúp người đọc định hướng.

activities.title: Avoid repetition with paraphrasing
activities.instruction_en: Rewrite using synonyms without changing the meaning.
activities.instruction_vi: Viết lại tránh lặp từ và giữ nguyên nghĩa.

items.question_en: Rewrite: “Famous people have advantages.”
items.question_vi: Diễn đạt lại câu người nổi tiếng có lợi ích.
items.explanation_en: Well-known corresponds to famous; benefits to advantages.
items.explanation_vi: Well-known/famous và benefits/advantages gần nghĩa.

items.question_en: Rewrite: “Celebrities often lose privacy.”
items.question_vi: Viết lại người nổi tiếng thường mất riêng tư.
items.answer: Public figures often have less personal privacy.
items.explanation_en: Public figures is a precise substitute for celebrities.
items.explanation_vi: Public figures là cách thay hợp lý.

items.question_en: Rewrite: “This is a disadvantage of being famous.”
items.question_vi: Diễn đạt bất lợi của nổi tiếng.
items.answer: This is a drawback of public recognition.
items.explanation_en: Drawback and public recognition avoid repetition.
items.explanation_vi: Dùng drawback và public recognition.

items.question_en: Why not replace “children” with “them” without a clear earlier noun?
items.question_vi: Vì sao không dùng them khi thiếu danh từ trước?
items.explanation_en: Pronouns need clear antecedents.
items.explanation_vi: Đại từ phải có từ được thay thế rõ ràng.

activities.title: Develop disadvantages of fame
activities.instruction_en: Build specific supporting points.
activities.instruction_vi: Phát triển luận điểm bất lợi với lý do cụ thể.

items.question_en: Which is a drawback: A loss of privacy B wider professional opportunities?
items.question_vi: Bất lợi là gì?
items.explanation_en: Privacy loss is harmful; opportunities are positive.
items.explanation_vi: Mất riêng tư tiêu cực, cơ hội nghề nghiệp tích cực.

items.question_en: Complete: “Constant photographs can make daily life ____.”
items.question_vi: Điền ảnh chụp liên tục khiến cuộc sống ____.
items.explanation_en: Stressful describes the life causing stress.
items.explanation_vi: Stressful miêu tả cuộc sống gây căng thẳng.

items.question_en: Give a specific example of unwanted publicity.
items.question_vi: Cho ví dụ cụ thể về sự chú ý không mong muốn.
items.answer: A photographer follows a singer to a family dinner.
items.explanation_en: A location, actor and action make the example concrete.
items.explanation_vi: Có người, địa điểm và hành động cụ thể.

items.question_en: How can a child be affected by publicity?
items.question_vi: Trẻ có thể bị ảnh hưởng thế nào?
items.answer: They may feel anxious when strangers discuss their private lives.
items.explanation_en: The example shows a plausible emotional consequence, not a universal fact.
items.explanation_vi: Đưa tác động tâm lý có thể xảy ra, không tuyệt đối hóa.

activities.title: Insert a relevant example
activities.instruction_en: Place examples after the point they illustrate.
activities.instruction_vi: Đặt ví dụ ngay sau luận điểm tương ứng.

items.question_en: Point: “Celebrity status can support charity.” Which example fits: A a concert funds a health clinic; B a singer buys shoes?
items.question_vi: Ví dụ nào hỗ trợ ý dùng danh tiếng làm từ thiện?
items.explanation_en: The concert funds a public benefit.
items.explanation_vi: Buổi hòa nhạc gây quỹ hỗ trợ cộng đồng.

items.question_en: Point: “Online criticism can harm wellbeing.” Which fits: A hurtful comments interrupt sleep; B posters are colourful?
items.question_vi: Ví dụ hỗ trợ tác động của bình luận độc hại?
items.explanation_en: It shows the effect of criticism.
items.explanation_vi: Cho thấy hậu quả của lời chỉ trích.

items.question_en: Use “For example” once in a sentence about a famous teacher.
items.question_vi: Viết một câu ví dụ về giáo viên nổi tiếng.
items.answer: For example, a popular teacher may provide free lessons to rural students.
items.explanation_en: For example introduces evidence, not the main claim.
items.explanation_vi: For example giới thiệu minh chứng, không phải luận điểm.

activities.title: Produce your own supporting evidence
activities.instruction_en: Use the pattern Point → Explanation → Example.
activities.instruction_vi: Tự viết minh chứng theo luận điểm → giải thích → ví dụ.

items.question_en: Support: “Well-known people can promote positive changes.”
items.question_vi: Hỗ trợ ý người nổi tiếng tạo thay đổi tích cực.
items.answer: A well-known athlete can encourage exercise. For example, their free online workouts may help beginners start training.
items.explanation_en: Link the example directly to the social benefit.
items.explanation_vi: Ví dụ phải nối trực tiếp với lợi ích xã hội.

items.question_en: Support: “Public attention can harm family life.”
items.question_vi: Hỗ trợ ý công chúng chú ý ảnh hưởng gia đình.
items.answer: A family may avoid ordinary outings because photographers follow them. For instance, a child might feel nervous at school.
items.explanation_en: Use an understandable consequence without sensational details.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu hệ quả dễ hiểu, không thêm chi tiết gây sốc.

items.question_en: Support: “Celebrity income can improve communities.”
items.question_vi: Hỗ trợ ý thu nhập người nổi tiếng giúp cộng đồng.
items.answer: An actor might fund books for a school library, giving more children access to reading.
items.explanation_en: The example shows a specific recipient and result.
items.explanation_vi: Có đối tượng hưởng lợi và kết quả.

activities.title: Pronouns for cohesion
activities.instruction_en: Replace repetition with clear pronouns.
activities.instruction_vi: Thay từ lặp bằng đại từ rõ nghĩa.

items.question_en: “Linh is a singer. Linh supports charities.” → ?
items.question_vi: Đổi lần nhắc Linh thứ hai.
items.explanation_en: She refers clearly to Linh.
items.explanation_vi: She thay cho Linh.

items.question_en: “The photographers arrived. The photographers waited outside.” → ?
items.question_vi: Thay photographers lần hai.
items.explanation_en: They refers to plural photographers.
items.explanation_vi: They thay danh từ số nhiều.

items.question_en: “I have three reasons. The first reason is privacy.” → ?
items.question_vi: Thay the first reason.
items.explanation_en: One replaces reason without repetition.
items.explanation_vi: One thay cho reason.

items.question_en: “The film became popular because the film was informative.” → ?
items.question_vi: Thay film lần hai.
items.answer: The film became popular because it was informative.
items.explanation_en: It clearly refers to the singular film.
items.explanation_vi: It thay the film.

items.question_en: “Celebrity children need safety. Celebrity children deserve privacy.” → ?
items.question_vi: Thay celebrity children lần hai.
items.explanation_en: They agrees with plural children.
items.explanation_vi: They phù hợp children số nhiều.

activities.title: Degrees of agreement
activities.instruction_en: Decide a position and maintain it throughout the essay.
activities.instruction_vi: Chọn mức độ đồng ý và giữ nhất quán.

items.question_en: “I tend to agree” means strong agreement or partial agreement?
items.question_vi: I tend to agree nghĩa đồng ý hoàn toàn hay phần nào?
items.explanation_en: Tend to signals a leaning rather than absolute agreement.
items.explanation_vi: Tend to biểu thị xu hướng, không tuyệt đối.

items.question_en: “I strongly disagree” = what position?
items.question_vi: I strongly disagree là quan điểm gì?
items.explanation_en: Strongly marks a high degree of disagreement.
items.explanation_vi: Strongly thể hiện mức độ phản đối cao.

items.question_en: Which opinion is relevant to limits on children’s photographs? A Protect children’s privacy B Buy cheaper cameras
items.question_vi: Ý phù hợp hạn chế ảnh trẻ em?
items.explanation_en: It directly concerns the stated protection issue.
items.explanation_vi: Đáp án bám nội dung bảo vệ trẻ.

items.question_en: State a balanced but clear view on celebrity privacy.
items.question_vi: Nêu quan điểm cân bằng nhưng rõ về riêng tư.
items.answer: I agree that public figures should have privacy, although reasonable reporting about their public work is acceptable.
items.explanation_en: A concession does not erase the main stance.
items.explanation_vi: Nhượng bộ không làm mất quan điểm chính.

activities.title: Analyse a Task 2 sample
activities.instruction_en: Identify topic sentence, support, counterargument and conclusion.
activities.instruction_vi: Nhận diện câu chủ đề, bằng chứng, quan điểm đối lập và kết luận.

items.question_en: Which is stronger: “Kids should be safe” or “Unwanted photos can reveal a child’s school location”?
items.question_vi: Câu nào cụ thể hơn?
items.answer: Unwanted photos can reveal a child’s school location.
items.explanation_en: It presents a measurable privacy risk.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu nguy cơ riêng tư cụ thể.

items.question_en: What is a counterargument?
items.question_vi: Counterargument nghĩa là gì?
items.answer: An opposing view considered by the writer.
items.explanation_en: A counterargument acknowledges another side.
items.explanation_vi: Là quan điểm đối lập được người viết xem xét.

items.question_en: In a four-paragraph essay, where should the final opinion appear?
items.question_vi: Ý kiến kết lại ở đâu?
items.explanation_en: The conclusion restates the position without a new main point.
items.explanation_vi: Kết luận nhắc lại lập trường, không mở ý lớn mới.

items.question_en: Should you invent statistics to make an example impressive? YES/NO
items.question_vi: Có nên bịa thống kê làm ví dụ?
items.explanation_en: Unsupported numerical claims weaken credibility.
items.explanation_vi: Số liệu tự bịa làm luận điểm thiếu tin cậy.

activities.title: Exam skills: full Task 2 practice
activities.instruction_en: Write a 250+ word essay, then review the model essays in the teacher guide.
activities.instruction_vi: Viết tối thiểu 250 từ rồi xem bài mẫu ở sách đáp án.

items.question_en: Task A: Does being famous bring more advantages than disadvantages? Give reasons and examples.
items.question_vi: Đề A: Nổi tiếng có lợi ích nhiều hơn bất lợi không?
items.answer: Suggested position: disadvantages outweigh the advantages because of privacy loss and stress, despite income and influence.
items.explanation_en: A clear position and developed examples matter more than difficult words.
items.explanation_vi: Quan điểm rõ và ví dụ triển khai quan trọng hơn dùng từ khó.

items.question_en: Task B: Photographs of celebrities’ children should not be published without permission. To what extent do you agree?
items.question_vi: Đề B: Không nên đăng ảnh con của người nổi tiếng khi chưa cho phép.
items.answer: Suggested position: strongly agree; argue safety and emotional wellbeing, then acknowledge consent-based family images.
items.explanation_en: Address the degree of agreement and opposing view.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu mức độ đồng ý, có cân nhắc ý đối lập.

items.question_en: Proofread: list three common mistakes and corrections for Task 2.
items.question_vi: Tự kiểm 3 lỗi phổ biến Task 2.
items.explanation_en: Check noun number, verb patterns and articles.
items.explanation_vi: Kiểm danh từ số nhiều, cấu trúc động từ và mạo từ.

activities.title: Lead-in: media vocabulary
activities.instruction_en: Identify the jobs or tools in the media.
activities.instruction_vi: Nhận dạng nghề và công cụ trong truyền thông.

items.question_en: A person who asks questions during a programme: reporter / tripod
items.question_vi: Người đặt câu hỏi trong chương trình?
items.explanation_en: Reporters conduct interviews and report stories.
items.explanation_vi: Phóng viên phỏng vấn và đưa tin.

items.question_en: A person responsible for making filming decisions: director / editor
items.question_vi: Người quyết định khi quay phim?
items.explanation_en: The director guides the film production.
items.explanation_vi: Đạo diễn chỉ đạo việc quay.

items.question_en: A tool used to stabilise a camera: tripod / microphone
items.question_vi: Công cụ giữ máy quay ổn định?
items.explanation_en: A tripod holds the camera firmly.
items.explanation_vi: Chân máy giữ máy ổn định.

items.question_en: An audio tool that records a voice: lens / microphone
items.question_vi: Công cụ thu tiếng?
items.explanation_en: A microphone captures sound.
items.explanation_vi: Micro thu âm.

activities.title: Flow-chart: a creator’s career
activities.instruction_en: Listen to Track A. Fill each gap with NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
activities.instruction_vi: Nghe Track A. Điền tối đa HAI TỪ mỗi chỗ.

items.question_en: 1 Iris first learned ____ at school.
items.question_vi: Iris học ____ tại trường.
items.explanation_en: The recording says she began by learning photography.
items.explanation_vi: Audio nói cô ấy học nhiếp ảnh trước tiên.

items.question_en: 2 Later, she taught herself ____.
items.question_vi: Sau đó cô tự học ____.
items.explanation_en: The exact two-word phrase is given.
items.explanation_vi: Cụm video editing được nghe đúng nguyên văn.

items.question_en: 3 Her first public video concerned a ____.
items.question_vi: Video đầu tiên của cô nói về ____.
items.explanation_en: “Community garden” is explicitly mentioned.
items.explanation_vi: Audio nêu đúng community garden.

items.question_en: 4 She won ____ in a film competition.
items.question_vi: Cô đạt ____ trong cuộc thi phim.
items.explanation_en: She won second, not first prize.
items.explanation_vi: Cô đạt giải nhì, không phải nhất.

items.question_en: 5 She attracted ____ of viewers.
items.question_vi: Cô thu hút ____ người xem.
items.explanation_en: The phrase “thousands of viewers” is heard.
items.explanation_vi: Nghe thousands of viewers.

items.question_en: 6 She later started a ____.
items.question_vi: Sau đó cô lập một ____.
items.explanation_en: The narrator rejects a television contract and names the company.
items.explanation_vi: Người dẫn phủ định hợp đồng TV và nêu lập công ty.

activities.title: Recognise listening distractors
activities.instruction_en: Identify information mentioned but NOT the final answer in Track A.
activities.instruction_vi: Nhận diện thông tin được nhắc nhưng không phải đáp án cuối.

items.question_en: Did Iris learn video editing from a college course? YES/NO
items.question_vi: Iris học video editing ở trường cao đẳng?
items.explanation_en: The speaker says she taught herself.
items.explanation_vi: Audio nêu cô tự học.

items.question_en: Did she win first prize? YES/NO
items.question_vi: Cô đạt giải nhất?
items.explanation_en: Second prize is the confirmed result.
items.explanation_vi: Giải nhì mới là thông tin đúng.

items.question_en: Was a TV contract signed? YES/NO
items.question_vi: Có ký hợp đồng truyền hình?
items.explanation_en: The narrator says she did not sign one.
items.explanation_vi: Người dẫn nói không ký.

items.question_en: Which is the LAST career step: production company / newspaper interview?
items.question_vi: Bước cuối là lập công ty hay được phỏng vấn báo?
items.explanation_en: The company step follows the interview.
items.explanation_vi: Lập công ty xảy ra sau phỏng vấn.

activities.title: Predict grammar before listening
activities.instruction_en: What type of word is missing?
activities.instruction_vi: Đoán loại từ cần điền trước khi nghe.

items.question_en: She learned ____ at school. Noun / verb?
items.question_vi: Chỗ trống sau learned là danh từ hay động từ?
items.explanation_en: A subject such as photography fits as object.
items.explanation_vi: Sau learned cần môn/kỹ năng dưới dạng danh từ.

items.question_en: She became very ____. Adjective / number?
items.question_vi: Sau became very cần gì?
items.explanation_en: Very generally modifies an adjective.
items.explanation_vi: Very thường bổ nghĩa tính từ.

items.question_en: She won ____ prize. Ordinal/verb?
items.question_vi: Trước prize cần gì?
items.explanation_en: An ordinal such as second specifies rank.
items.explanation_vi: Số thứ tự như second chỉ hạng.

items.question_en: She set up a small ____. Noun / adjective?
items.question_vi: Sau a small cần gì?
items.explanation_en: A small modifies a following noun.
items.explanation_vi: Small là tính từ bổ nghĩa danh từ sau.

items.question_en: She spoke ____. Adverb / noun?
items.question_vi: Sau spoke có thể cần gì?
items.explanation_en: An adverb can explain how she spoke.
items.explanation_vi: Trạng từ chỉ cách nói.

activities.title: Listening to opinions about fame
activities.instruction_en: Listen to Track B. Fill gaps with NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
activities.instruction_vi: Nghe Track B, điền tối đa hai từ.

items.question_en: 1 Mia fears losing her ____.
items.question_vi: Mia sợ mất ____.
items.explanation_en: She explicitly says “lose my privacy”.
items.explanation_vi: Nghe lose my privacy.

items.question_vi: Bị chụp ảnh lúc mua sắm khiến cô thấy ____.
items.explanation_en: Mia calls the situation stressful.

items.question_vi: Leo hy vọng biểu diễn ở ____ lớn.

items.explanation_vi: Leo nói large theatres.

items.question_vi: Leo muốn gặp các ____.
items.explanation_en: He names fellow musicians.
items.explanation_vi: Đáp án trực tiếp musicians.

items.question_en: 5 Leo would donate money to a ____.
items.question_vi: Leo quyên tiền cho một ____.
items.explanation_en: Music school is exactly two words.
items.explanation_vi: Music school vừa 2 từ.

items.question_en: 6 Mia prefers quiet ____.
items.question_vi: Mia thích ____ yên tĩnh.
items.explanation_en: Her last line says quiet weekends.
items.explanation_vi: Câu cuối của Mia: quiet weekends.

activities.title: Flow-chart: build a reliable blog
activities.instruction_en: Listen to Track C and complete each step in order. NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
activities.instruction_vi: Nghe C, điền tối đa hai từ theo đúng thứ tự.

items.question_en: Step 1: Choose a ____ you know.
items.question_vi: Bước 1 chọn ____ mình hiểu.
items.explanation_en: “Choose a subject you know well.”
items.explanation_vi: Chọn chủ đề mình nắm rõ.

items.question_en: Step 2: Study your ____.
items.question_vi: Bước 2 tìm hiểu ____.
items.explanation_en: The presenter says study your audience.
items.explanation_vi: Nghe study your audience.

items.question_en: Step 3: Create a publishing ____.
items.question_vi: Bước 3 lập ____ đăng bài.
items.explanation_en: “Simple publishing schedule.”
items.explanation_vi: Nghe publishing schedule.

items.question_en: Step 4: Check your ____ before posting.
items.question_vi: Bước 4 kiểm tra ____ trước đăng.
items.explanation_en: The presenter says check your facts.
items.explanation_vi: Nghe check your facts.

items.question_en: Step 5: Learn from ____.
items.question_vi: Bước 5 học từ ____.
items.explanation_en: The last step is learn from feedback.
items.explanation_vi: Bước cuối đúng là feedback.

activities.title: Verify flow order and accuracy
activities.instruction_en: Use Track C and correct inaccurate notes.
activities.instruction_vi: Dựa vào Track C để sửa ghi chú sai.

items.question_en: Correct: “Publish every day.”
items.question_vi: Sửa “Đăng bài mỗi ngày.”
items.answer: You do not need to post every day; be consistent.
items.explanation_en: Consistency, not daily posting, is recommended.
items.explanation_vi: Người nói khuyên đều đặn, không bắt buộc mỗi ngày.

items.question_en: Correct: “Hide errors to protect your reputation.”
items.question_vi: Sửa “Giấu lỗi để giữ danh tiếng.”
items.explanation_en: The speaker explicitly says not to hide them.
items.explanation_vi: Audio khuyên công khai sửa lỗi.

items.question_en: Correct: “A shocking headline is more valuable than facts.”
items.question_vi: Sửa “Tiêu đề giật gân quý hơn sự thật.”
items.answer: Reliable information is more valuable than a shocking headline.
items.explanation_en: The original sentence reverses the comparison.
items.explanation_vi: Câu sai đảo ngược ý so sánh.

items.question_en: Does the narrator recommend studying audience questions? YES/NO
items.question_vi: Người nói khuyên đọc câu hỏi của độc giả?
items.explanation_en: Step two explicitly includes their questions.
items.explanation_vi: Bước hai yêu cầu xem câu hỏi.

activities.title: Technical and scientific vocabulary
activities.instruction_en: Predict meanings in a camera training talk.
activities.instruction_vi: Học nghĩa từ kỹ thuật trước khi nghe bài máy quay.

items.question_en: Aperture means: A opening for light B battery size C audio cable
items.question_vi: Aperture là gì?
items.explanation_en: An aperture is an adjustable opening in a lens system.
items.explanation_vi: Aperture là khẩu độ, lỗ mở điều chỉnh ánh sáng.

items.question_en: Focus means: A make the image sharp B add a soundtrack C make the lens heavy
items.question_vi: Focus nghĩa là gì?
items.explanation_en: Focusing changes image clarity.
items.explanation_vi: Lấy nét làm ảnh rõ.

items.question_en: Tripod means: A camera stand B camera screen C recorder file
items.question_vi: Tripod là gì?
items.explanation_en: A tripod is a three-legged support.
items.explanation_vi: Tripod là giá ba chân.

items.question_en: Zoom means: A change subject size in frame B delete image C switch microphone
items.question_vi: Zoom nghĩa là gì?
items.explanation_en: Zoom changes framing or apparent subject size.
items.explanation_vi: Zoom thay đổi khung hình/kích thước chủ thể.

items.question_en: A “shaky picture” is: A unstable B bright C silent
items.question_vi: Shaky picture nghĩa là gì?
items.explanation_en: Shaky refers to unwanted camera movement.
items.explanation_vi: Shaky chỉ ảnh rung.

activities.title: Synonyms in technical explanations
activities.instruction_en: Match a phrase to its equivalent.
activities.instruction_vi: Ghép từ/cụm từ tương đương.

items.question_en: “sharp” ≈ A clear B loud
items.question_vi: Sharp gần nghĩa gì?
items.explanation_en: A sharp image has clear detail.
items.explanation_vi: Ảnh sharp có chi tiết sắc nét.

items.question_en: “wider opening” ≈ A larger aperture B lower volume
items.question_vi: Wider opening gần nghĩa?
items.explanation_en: Both refer to an aperture allowing more light.
items.explanation_vi: Cả hai chỉ khẩu độ mở lớn.

items.question_en: “steady image” ≈ A stable shot B noisy recording
items.question_vi: Steady image gần nghĩa?
items.explanation_en: Stable means little unwanted movement.
items.explanation_vi: Stable là ổn định, ít rung.

items.question_en: “close to” ≈ A near B behind
items.question_vi: Close to gần nghĩa?
items.explanation_en: Near expresses short distance.
items.explanation_vi: Near là ở gần.

items.question_en: “fully charged” ≈ A full battery B broken lens
items.question_vi: Fully charged gần nghĩa?
items.explanation_en: It describes a battery with full charge.
items.explanation_vi: Pin đã được sạc đầy.

activities.title: Flow-chart: camera operation
activities.instruction_en: Listen to Track D. Complete with NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
activities.instruction_vi: Nghe Track D và điền tối đa hai từ.

items.question_en: 1 Use ____ controls for advanced filming.
items.question_vi: Sử dụng điều khiển ____ khi quay nâng cao.
items.explanation_en: The opening contrasts automatic and manual settings.
items.explanation_vi: Audio đối chiếu tự động và chỉnh tay.

items.question_en: 2 Turn the focus ring until the face looks ____.
items.question_vi: Vặn vòng lấy nét tới khi mặt ____.
items.explanation_en: “Face looks sharp” is stated directly.
items.explanation_vi: Đúng từ sharp.

items.question_en: 3 The aperture controls the amount of ____.
items.question_vi: Khẩu độ kiểm soát lượng ____.
items.explanation_en: It controls how much light enters the lens.
items.explanation_vi: Nó kiểm soát ánh sáng vào ống kính.

items.question_en: 4 A wider opening makes the image appear ____.
items.question_vi: Mở rộng khẩu độ làm ảnh ____ hơn.
items.explanation_en: The speaker says “may appear brighter”.
items.explanation_vi: Nghe may appear brighter.

items.question_en: 5 For a long interview, use a ____.
items.question_vi: Phỏng vấn dài nên dùng ____.
items.explanation_en: Tripod prevents shaking.
items.explanation_vi: Chân máy giảm rung.

items.question_en: 6 Too much zoom makes small ____ more obvious.
items.question_vi: Zoom nhiều khiến ____ nhỏ lộ rõ.
items.explanation_en: The exact plural noun movements is heard.
items.explanation_vi: Audio dùng movements số nhiều.

items.question_en: 7 Check the microphone and the ____.
items.question_vi: Kiểm micro và ____.
items.explanation_en: The last sentence mentions the battery.
items.explanation_vi: Câu cuối nhắc pin.

activities.title: Exam: how to make a short film
activities.instruction_en: Listen to Track E, then fill the seven stages. NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
activities.instruction_vi: Nghe E, điền 7 bước tối đa hai từ.

items.question_en: 1 Decide who the ____ will be.
items.question_vi: Xác định ____ của bộ phim.
items.explanation_en: The first step is the intended audience.
items.explanation_vi: Bước đầu xác định người xem.

items.question_en: 2 Write a simple story ____.
items.question_vi: Viết ____ câu chuyện đơn giản.
items.explanation_en: The lecturer explicitly says story outline.
items.explanation_vi: Nghe story outline.

items.question_en: 3 Decide on your ____.
items.question_vi: Quyết định về ____.
items.explanation_en: Costs are discussed immediately after the word budget.
items.explanation_vi: Sau budget là các ví dụ chi phí.

items.question_en: 4 Write a script describing each ____.
items.question_vi: Viết kịch bản mô tả từng ____.
items.explanation_en: The lecturer defines each scene and dialogue.
items.explanation_vi: Giảng viên nêu cảnh phim.

items.question_en: 5 Draw a ____ with simple pictures.
items.question_vi: Vẽ ____ bằng hình đơn giản.
items.explanation_en: Storyboard is directly defined by the speaker.
items.explanation_vi: Audio giải thích storyboard.

items.question_en: 6 Choose a ____ to make filming decisions.
items.question_vi: Chọn ____ ra quyết định khi quay.
items.explanation_en: A director makes decisions while filming.
items.explanation_vi: Đạo diễn quyết định trong quá trình quay.

items.question_en: 7 Arrange a ____ before recording.
items.question_vi: Sắp xếp ____ trước lúc quay.
items.explanation_en: Final step is a rehearsal.
items.explanation_vi: Bước cuối là buổi diễn tập.

activities.title: Lead-in: describe influential people
activities.instruction_en: Use accurate adjectives and reasons.
activities.instruction_vi: Dùng tính từ mô tả nhân vật có ảnh hưởng và nêu lý do.

items.question_en: Which adjective describes someone who gives money to others: generous / cruel?
items.question_vi: Người hay giúp đỡ cho đi tiền là?
items.explanation_en: Generous means willing to give and help.
items.explanation_vi: Generous là hào phóng.

items.question_en: “A ____ musician” — talented / talent?
items.question_vi: Điền tính từ trước musician.
items.explanation_en: A descriptive adjective goes before the noun.
items.explanation_vi: Dùng tính từ talented trước danh từ.

items.question_en: Which is a skill adjective: experienced / experience?
items.question_vi: Tính từ chỉ có kinh nghiệm?
items.explanation_en: Experienced works as an adjective.
items.explanation_vi: Experienced là tính từ.

items.question_en: “She is very ____ because she tells the truth.”
items.question_vi: Cô ấy ____ vì nói thật.
items.explanation_en: Honest describes truthfulness.
items.explanation_vi: Honest nghĩa trung thực.

items.question_en: Describe one person you admire using two adjectives and a reason.
items.question_vi: Mô tả người bạn ngưỡng mộ bằng 2 tính từ và lý do.
items.answer: I admire a local teacher because she is patient and knowledgeable, and she helps beginners understand difficult lessons.
items.explanation_en: An effective answer links traits to a specific action.
items.explanation_vi: Đáp án tốt nối đặc điểm với việc làm cụ thể.

activities.title: Speaking Part 2: understand the cue card
activities.instruction_en: Plan: who / why famous / when you saw them / why you admire them.
activities.instruction_vi: Lập dàn ý 4 điểm: ai / vì sao nổi tiếng / gặp khi nào / vì sao ngưỡng mộ.

items.question_en: Who is the person?
items.question_vi: Nhân vật là ai?
items.answer: A science teacher who shares clear lessons online.
items.explanation_en: Choose someone you can describe naturally.
items.explanation_vi: Chọn người dễ kể tự nhiên.

items.question_en: Why is the person famous?
items.question_vi: Vì sao người này nổi tiếng?
items.answer: Her short tutorials make complicated topics easy to understand.
items.explanation_en: Focus on work or achievements rather than unsupported private details.
items.explanation_vi: Nói về thành tựu, tránh suy đoán đời tư.

items.question_en: Where and when did you first see this person?
items.question_vi: Bạn biết đến họ khi nào/ở đâu?
items.answer: I first saw her videos on a learning channel two years ago.
items.explanation_en: Past simple fits a finished first meeting.
items.explanation_vi: Dùng quá khứ đơn với lần đầu gặp có mốc.

items.question_en: Give three reasons why you admire the person.
items.question_vi: Nêu ba lý do ngưỡng mộ.
items.answer: She is patient, honest and willing to explain challenging ideas.
items.explanation_en: Three developed points are better than three isolated adjectives.
items.explanation_vi: Ba ý có triển khai tốt hơn ba tính từ rời.

items.question_en: End with a personal effect.
items.question_vi: Kết bằng tác động đến bản thân.
items.answer: Her videos encourage me to check sources and keep learning.
items.explanation_en: The ending returns to the feeling of admiration.
items.explanation_vi: Kết luận nhấn lại lý do ngưỡng mộ.

activities.title: Connect ideas with linking words
activities.instruction_en: Choose because, although, when, who, whose, and, but, so.
activities.instruction_vi: Chọn từ nối phù hợp để liên kết câu.

items.question_en: I admire her ____ she helps learners.
items.question_vi: Ngưỡng mộ vì cô giúp học viên.
items.explanation_en: Because introduces reason.
items.explanation_vi: Because mở lý do.

items.question_en: He is a singer ____ performs in local theatres.
items.question_vi: Ca sĩ ____ biểu diễn ở rạp địa phương.
items.explanation_en: Who refers to a person as subject.
items.explanation_vi: Who thay cho người làm chủ ngữ.

items.question_en: She became known ____ she posted a useful series.
items.question_vi: Cô nổi tiếng ____ đăng chuỗi bài hữu ích.
items.explanation_en: When introduces the time.
items.explanation_vi: When chỉ thời điểm.

items.question_en: He is talented, ____ he does not enjoy public attention.
items.question_vi: Anh tài năng, ____ không thích chú ý.
items.explanation_en: But adds contrast.
items.explanation_vi: But nối ý trái ngược.

items.question_en: She works hard, ____ her videos improve each month.
items.question_vi: Cô làm việc chăm, ____ video cải thiện.
items.explanation_en: So presents the result.
items.explanation_vi: So nêu kết quả.

items.question_en: The author ____ blog I read is a doctor.
items.question_vi: Tác giả ____ blog tôi đọc là bác sĩ.
items.explanation_en: Whose marks possession.
items.explanation_vi: Whose chỉ sở hữu.

items.question_en: ____ she is popular, she stays polite.
items.question_vi: ____ cô nổi tiếng, cô vẫn lịch sự.
items.explanation_en: Although introduces concession.
items.explanation_vi: Although mở nhượng bộ.

activities.title: One-minute cue-card notes
activities.instruction_en: Write keywords, not full sentences.
activities.instruction_vi: Ghi chú từ khóa trong một phút, không viết nguyên câu.

items.question_en: Notes for WHO?
items.question_vi: Ghi chú AI?
items.explanation_en: Short noun phrases save preparation time.
items.explanation_vi: Cụm danh từ ngắn tiết kiệm thời gian.

items.question_en: Notes for WHY FAMOUS?
items.question_vi: Ghi chú VÌ SAO?
items.explanation_en: Two keywords can guide a full sentence.
items.explanation_vi: Hai từ khóa dẫn tới câu đầy đủ.

items.question_en: Notes for WHEN/WHERE?
items.question_vi: Ghi chú KHI NÀO / Ở ĐÂU?
items.explanation_en: A time and place cover the cue point.
items.explanation_vi: Một thời gian và nơi chốn đáp ứng ý.

items.question_en: Notes for WHY ADMIRE?
items.question_vi: Ghi chú VÌ SAO NGƯỠNG MỘ?
items.explanation_en: List three reasons to elaborate later.
items.explanation_vi: Ba từ khóa để triển khai khi nói.

activities.title: Extend a two-minute talk
activities.instruction_en: Practise with a model and add reasons/examples.
activities.instruction_vi: Luyện bài khoảng 2 phút, mở rộng bằng lý do và ví dụ.

items.question_en: Extend “She is kind” by adding an example.
items.question_vi: Mở rộng “Cô ấy tốt bụng” với ví dụ.
items.answer: She is kind because she replies politely to beginners and encourages them when they make mistakes.
items.explanation_en: A reason and a behaviour develop the description.
items.explanation_vi: Thêm lý do và hành vi minh họa.

items.question_en: Extend “I saw her online” with time and result.
items.question_vi: Mở rộng “Tôi thấy cô ấy trên mạng” với mốc và tác động.
items.answer: I saw her online about two years ago, and her lessons helped me become more confident.
items.explanation_en: When plus personal impact creates a connected answer.
items.explanation_vi: Có mốc và tác động cá nhân, câu liên kết tốt.

items.question_en: Add one concluding sentence to a Part 2 talk.
items.question_vi: Viết câu kết cho Part 2.
items.answer: Overall, I admire her because she uses her popularity to help other people learn.
items.explanation_en: Finish by restating the central reason.
items.explanation_vi: Kết quay lại lý do cốt lõi.

items.question_en: Use past and present tenses accurately in one short answer.
items.question_vi: Dùng quá khứ và hiện tại đúng trong một câu.
items.answer: I discovered her channel in 2024, and I still watch it today.
items.explanation_en: Discovered marks a finished time; watch describes a present habit.
items.explanation_vi: Discovered là quá khứ có mốc; watch là thói quen hiện tại.

activities.title: Speaking Part 3: types of questions
activities.instruction_en: Match a question to the cognitive function.
activities.instruction_vi: Ghép câu hỏi với yêu cầu tư duy.

items.question_en: “Why do people follow famous actors?” Explain/opine/predict?
items.question_vi: Vì sao người ta theo dõi diễn viên?
items.explanation_en: Why asks for causes or reasons.
items.explanation_vi: Why yêu cầu lý do.

items.question_en: “How did celebrities influence society in the past compared with today?”
items.question_vi: So sánh xưa và nay thuộc dạng gì?
items.explanation_en: Compared with asks for similarities and differences.
items.explanation_vi: Compared with yêu cầu so sánh.

items.question_en: “Will anyone become famous through new technology?”
items.question_vi: Dạng hỏi tương lai?
items.explanation_en: Will invites a future prediction.
items.explanation_vi: Will yêu cầu dự đoán.

items.question_en: “Should famous people have private lives?”
items.question_vi: Dạng bày tỏ quan điểm?
items.explanation_en: Should asks for a position.
items.explanation_vi: Should thường yêu cầu lập trường.

items.question_en: “What problems can fame cause?”
items.question_vi: Dạng nêu vấn đề?
items.explanation_en: The question requires specific negative consequences.
items.explanation_vi: Phải nêu hệ quả tiêu cực cụ thể.

activities.title: Part 3: match questions and model ideas
activities.instruction_en: Identify a suitable main idea for each prompt.
activities.instruction_vi: Ghép câu hỏi và ý trả lời phù hợp.

items.question_en: Question: Why do people follow celebrities? Idea: A entertainment and inspiration B better traffic
items.question_vi: Ý phù hợp lý do theo dõi người nổi tiếng?
items.explanation_en: Entertainment and inspiration directly answer why.
items.explanation_vi: Giải trí và cảm hứng trả lời đúng vì sao.

items.question_en: Question: How has fame changed? Idea: A traditional media versus online platforms B different school uniforms
items.question_vi: Ý phù hợp sự thay đổi của danh tiếng?

activities.title: Exam skills: original Part 3 answers
activities.instruction_en: Speak two or three developed sentences per question, with examples.
activities.instruction_vi: Nói 2–3 câu có lý do, ví dụ cho mỗi câu.

items.question_en: Why do some people want to become famous?
items.question_vi: Vì sao một số người muốn nổi tiếng?
items.answer: Some people hope for financial success and the chance to influence others. For example, a talented musician may want their songs to reach a larger audience.
items.explanation_en: State two motives and illustrate one.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu hai động cơ rồi minh họa một.

items.question_en: Is it easier to become famous today than in the past?
items.question_vi: Ngày nay dễ nổi tiếng hơn trước?
items.answer: It may be easier to get noticed because anyone can post videos online. However, it can be harder to remain popular because so many people create content.
items.explanation_en: Balance access with competition using a contrast.
items.explanation_vi: So sánh cơ hội tiếp cận và cạnh tranh.

items.question_en: Should famous people be role models?
items.question_vi: Người nổi tiếng có nên là hình mẫu?
items.answer: Some can be good role models when they work hard and behave responsibly. But popularity alone does not make somebody a good example for children.
items.explanation_en: Qualify the claim; popularity is not character.
items.explanation_vi: Nêu điều kiện, không đồng nhất nổi tiếng với nhân cách.

items.question_en: What kinds of people may become famous in the future?
items.question_vi: Ai có thể nổi tiếng trong tương lai?
items.answer: I think online educators and creators who solve everyday problems may attract more attention. Useful content can build a loyal audience over time.
items.explanation_en: Predict and explain rather than listing names.
items.explanation_vi: Dự đoán và giải thích thay vì liệt kê tên.

items.question_en: How can journalists report on celebrities responsibly?
items.question_vi: Nhà báo đưa tin người nổi tiếng có trách nhiệm thế nào?
items.answer: They should verify information and focus on public activities. They should also avoid sharing private details about children without permission.
items.explanation_en: Use should + base verb for advice.
items.explanation_vi: Dùng should + V nguyên mẫu để khuyên.

writing_models.title: Advantages and disadvantages of fame (about 285 words)
writing_models.question: Does being famous have more advantages or disadvantages?
writing_models.text:
Some people dream of becoming famous because they expect an exciting and comfortable life. Although public recognition can create valuable opportunities, I believe that its disadvantages are often more serious than people imagine.

One clear advantage is that successful public figures may earn a high income. This money can give them financial security and allow them to support worthwhile projects. For example, a popular musician might use the profits from a concert to pay for instruments at a local school. Fame can also help a person communicate an important message. An environmental campaign led by a well-known actor may attract people who would otherwise ignore the issue.

However, the loss of privacy is a major drawback. Celebrities may find it difficult to visit ordinary places without being photographed. Constant public attention can create stress and make family relationships harder to manage. Another problem is that online comments can be extremely critical. Even when a public figure makes a small mistake, thousands of strangers may discuss it. This pressure can affect both the individual and their relatives, including children who have not chosen to be in the public eye.

Some people argue that famous people simply have to accept these difficulties because attention is part of their career. I partly understand this view, but public interest should have reasonable limits. People should be judged mainly on their work rather than on every detail of their personal lives.

In conclusion, fame can bring money, influence and professional opportunities, but the risks to privacy and wellbeing are substantial. For this reason, I consider the disadvantages to be greater overall.
writing_models.vi: Bài 4 đoạn: mở bài nêu lập trường bất lợi nhiều hơn; đoạn 2 lợi ích và ví dụ; đoạn 3 bất lợi và hậu quả; đoạn 4 nhượng bộ có giới hạn; kết luận khẳng định. Lưu ý không học thuộc nguyên bài.

writing_models.title: Should young celebrities be protected? (about 280 words)
writing_models.question: Photographs of celebrities’ children should not be published without permission. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
writing_models.text:
The children of famous people sometimes appear in newspapers and on social media simply because their parents are well known. I strongly agree that images of these children should not be published without appropriate permission, especially when the photographs reveal private details.

The strongest reason is that children cannot fully understand the long-term consequences of being recognised by strangers. A photograph of a child outside a school, for instance, might show where the child spends time every day. If it spreads online, it may create unnecessary safety concerns for the family. Children should be able to grow up without feeling watched whenever they leave home.

Another reason is that repeated media attention may affect a child's confidence and wellbeing. People can make unkind comments about a person's appearance, clothes or behaviour, even when that person is very young. A child who reads such comments might become anxious or embarrassed. Protecting privacy gives children more freedom to make mistakes and enjoy ordinary experiences while they are growing up.

Admittedly, public figures sometimes choose to share family photographs to celebrate an event or support a good cause. In such cases, carefully selected images may be acceptable when the child's interests are protected. Nevertheless, this is very different from strangers taking pictures without consent or publishing a child's location.

In conclusion, the public may be curious about the families of celebrities, but curiosity is not a good enough reason to ignore children's privacy. Clear rules and responsible media behaviour would help protect young people who did not choose to become famous.

speaking_models.title: Speaking Part 2: a famous educator I admire
speaking_models.text:
I am going to describe a person whose educational videos I really admire. She is a Vietnamese science teacher who explains difficult topics in a simple and friendly way. I first came across her channel when I was preparing for an important examination, and I have followed her work since then.

She is known for short lessons that use everyday examples instead of complicated language. In one video, she used a cup of hot water to explain a scientific idea. It was such an ordinary object, but her explanation helped me remember the lesson much more easily.

There are three main reasons why I admire her. Firstly, she is patient and makes learning enjoyable. Secondly, she encourages students to check information carefully rather than believe everything they read online. Finally, she is willing to admit when she makes a mistake, which I think is an important quality in a teacher.

I have never met her in person, but her videos have helped me become more confident in my studies. If I could talk to her one day, I would thank her for sharing her knowledge with so many learners. I admire her not because she is famous, but because she uses her popularity to help other people.
